title: BGN with a priced AR(1) state y and three exposure types: vyg25's construction in BGN
question: Does a priced second factor with heterogeneous firm exposures create a fair complexity gap in BGN, as it does in KP14?
notes:
THE KP14 CONSTRUCTION ONE MODEL OVER (2026-10-07). vyg25 is the project's only KP14 economy with a fair gap positive in ten seeds of ten (+0.0148), and its mechanism -- a priced stationary state y, three firm types loading cash flows as e^{b_f y}, a y=0 level compensation bv_comp 1.2, price gamma_v 2.5, kappa_y 0.35 -- had never been built in BGN or GS21: BGN has no firm type at all (its project-beta continuum is the same distribution for every firm) and GS21's exposure path (gx7, bx7) loaded types on the EXISTING state x, not on a new priced one. This spec adds exactly vyg25's ingredients.

LADDER. KP14's type_bv (0.02/0.07/0.14) HALVED. Calibration on a 120-firm panel (validate_bgn_vy.py, 2026-10-07 22:50 CDT): at the literal KP ladder the type premia are 9.0/15.3/26.0 %/yr with SR_max 0.60 and a mean premium of 17 %/yr -- far above the 4-11 %/yr band every reported economy sits in; at the halved ladder they are 8.7/11.7/16.5 %/yr (bgnbase: 8.4 on the same panel, 7.0 over ten seeds) with SR_max 0.49, which is vyg25's 0.495. The halved ladder is the one whose attainable Sharpe matches the economy it copies. type_theta (1, 1.115, 1.293); the regime block is inert at gmult [1,1].

CHECKS BEFORE SUBMISSION. Project-value Euler equation with y: worst 2e-14 at every (r, y, beta, s, type). J* fixed-point residual 9e-8. Reduction to bgn_gam at zero exposure on one seed: prices within 1.9e-3 (the DP against the closed form's 950-period truncation), expected returns within 2e-5, SR_max to 1e-4. Realised vs expected by type within 2.3 se on the calibration panel, the same offset the zero-exposure economy shows on that seed.

PRECOMMITMENT STATUS: precommitted=false. The producer is new and the working tree is dirty (the other Quest work), so precommit_spec.py refuses; the id is read from the Quest build log by fill_spec_ids.py and this spec is the record of the parameters BEFORE the seeds ran.

PREDICTION (2026-10-07, before the run). The reduced-form screen says only static curvature of the premium in the ranks, priced, makes a fair gap; a y-exposure ladder in BGN is a LEVEL sort (type_theta) with a y-rotating premium, i.e. the BGN/GS state signature (room mostly linear-in-state, linrank_s takes it). So: room above bgnbase's +0.027 (expect +0.05 to +0.10, SR_max about 0.49), room_s well below room, fair gap between -0.005 and +0.010, NOT above vyg25's +0.0148. FALSIFIED as 'the KP mechanism ports' if the fair gap exceeds +0.010 in 8 of 10 seeds; CONFIRMED as a BGN-signature economy if room_s/room < 0.5.

changes: new model directory variants/bgn_vy (nests bgn_gam at type_bv [0]; gmult [1,1] inert)
y: AR(1) kappa_y 0.35/yr, unit sd, priced at gamma_v 2.5 (per unit Brownian per sqrt-year, kp_vy's convention)
three types in shares [0.34, 0.33, 0.33] with exposures [0.01, 0.035, 0.07], bv_comp 1.2
J*_f(r, y, s) solved as a dynamic programme (321 x dy/4 grid, tol 1e-7)

seeds.policy: run_oracle.py --seed drives BOTH the firm-level shocks (global numpy stream) and the AGGREGATE state path (gam_seed / bx_seed / reg_seed offset by the seed). Seed 0 reproduces the single-run behaviour; --common_aggregate restores the fixed-aggregate behaviour as an explicit variance decomposition.
